description: Seven SEM micrographs (panels b–h; panel a of the original a–h series is not supplied in this group), all of the medium-Mn low-density steels in different aging states. Each panel carries a white 20 µm scale bar at bottom right and a top-right state label: "as-cast" (e), "723 K/3 h" (b, f), "773 K/3 h" (c, g), "823 K/3 h" (d, h). Per the caption, (b–d) are the 0.02Nb steel and (e–h) the 0.04Nb steel. In every panel the matrix is marked γ (austenite, mid-grey) and a yellow δ label with yellow arrows points to irregularly shaped, brighter-etched, vermicular/dendritic ferrite islands randomly dispersed in that matrix; sparse submicron white particles are marked by purple arrows. Ferrite shape, distribution and apparent area fraction look similar across all seven panels and across both Nb levels, and no numeric ferrite content is printed on any image. The group demonstrates that the irregular δ-ferrite dispersion in the γ matrix is essentially unaffected by Nb content (0.02 vs 0.04 wt%) or by aging at 723–823 K for 3 h, while Nb addition produces the white particles marked by the purple arrows.

observations.observation: Every supplied panel is a SEM micrograph with a white 20 µm scale bar at the bottom right.
Top-right state labels read "as-cast" (e), "723 K/3 h" (b, f), "773 K/3 h" (c, g) and "823 K/3 h" (d, h).
The austenite matrix is labelled with a yellow "γ" in each micrograph.
A yellow "δ" label with yellow arrows points to irregularly shaped, brighter-etched ferrite islands dispersed in the matrix in all panels.
Purple arrows mark sparse submicron white particles located within the austenite matrix, most clearly in (d), (g) and (h).
The ferrite morphology and its apparent area fraction appear similar in all seven panels regardless of aging temperature or Nb level; no numeric ferrite content is printed on any image.
Panel (a) of the a–h series is not present in this image group; only (b)–(h) were supplied.
The caption states that panels a–d are the 0.02Nb steels and panels e–h the 0.04Nb steels, at different aging states.
The citing text states that irregular-shaped ferrite is randomly dispersed within the austenite matrix.

The citing text states measured ferrite contents of ≈16.2 vol% (as-cast), 16.4, 17.1 and 18.3 vol% after aging at 723, 773 and 823 K for 3 h in the 0.02Nb steel, and 16.3, 17.2, 18.4 and 18.1 vol% for the 0.04Nb steel under the same states.
The citing text states that Nb addition leads to submicron white particles within the austenite matrix, indicated by the purple arrows in Figure 2.
The citing text concludes that the ferrite contents are not affected by the aging temperature, consistent with the XRD analysis.
